body: Finding (macOS, Blocks-candidate for VoiceOver users): closing the Calendar month picker crashes the app when macOS accessibility is on.U+000AU+000AU+002D Symptom: SIGSEGV (EXC_BAD_ACCESS at 0x48) in FlutterMacOS `flutter::AccessibilityBridge::CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate()` U+003C `CommitUpdates()` U+003C `-[FlutterViewController updateSemantics:]`, on the main thread, the moment the picker closes.U+000AU+002D Reproduced 5 of 5: Escape (twice), picking a month (Jun), clicking outside (Dismiss month picker), and "Back to this week". Control with accessibility off: Escape and picking Jun close it with no crash.U+000AU+002D How accessibility was switched on: the scratch runner posts `NSApplicationDidChangeAccessibilityEnhancedUserInterfaceNotification` with AXEnhancedUserInterface=true when launched with PROBE_AX=1, which is the notification VoiceOver's AXEnhancedUserInterface causes; FlutterEngine.onAccessibilityStatusChanged then sets semanticsEnabled. The first crash (00:35:42) happened unprompted after an AX-tree read had flipped the same switch. Real VoiceOver was not turned on (system setting), so the VoiceOver claim is by code path, not observed speech.U+000AU+002D Suspect (unverified): `lib/features/calendar/calendar_screen.dart` `_buildPicker` wraps the overlay in `BlockSemantics` with a `CompositedTransformFollower`; removing it reparents nodes, which the macOS bridge mishandles. The crash itself is inside the Flutter engine (a null dereference), so a Flutter bug is likely, triggered by this tree shape. This is the same wrapper the Android sweep found empty on the phone.U+000AU+002D Evidence: results/macos/e2e/field_notes_probe-2026-09-27-0035*.ips, -003714, -003800, -003806, -003814; m1_ax_picker_open.png.U+000AU+002D Separate observation: with accessibility off, macOS's AX tree for the window holds only the three window buttons; Flutter content appears to assistive tech only once the switch is on. The live-tree sweep therefore uses PROBE_AX=1.
